successors.text: Susiana and the Elamite highland: 'In 540 BC, Achaemenid rule began in Susa'

ledger.x: 3200 BCE: Proto-Elamite Susa.
2700 BCE: the Old Elamite period begins ('Old Elamite: c.
2500 BCE: the dynasty of Awan.
2450 BCE: Eannatum of Lagash overruns Elam.
2425 BCE: Lagash's hold on Elam lapses with Eannatum's death (Enannatum I 'r. c.
2290 BCE: Susa becomes Akkad's vassal.
2240 BCE: Kutik-Inshushinak unites Susa and Anshan.
2210 BCE: Susa is free of Akkad.
2125 BCE (bridged): Puzur-Inshushinak (Kutik-Inshushinak) takes Akkad from the Gutians, who held it from -2154.
2125 BCE (bridged): Eshnunna and the Diyala cities, taken in the same campaigns.
2100 BCE: the Shimashki dynasty.
2100 BCE: Ur-Nammu 'reconquered the northern territories'.
2094 BCE: Ur takes Susa.
2015 BCE: Susa slips from Ur.
2004 BCE: Kindattu sacks Ur and settles there.
1983 BCE: Ishbi-Erra of Isin expels the Elamite garrison from Ur.
1970 BCE: the Sukkalmah (Epartid) dynasty.
1767 BCE: Siwe-palar-huppak invades Eshnunna.
1760 BCE: 'Around 1760 BC, Hammurabi drove out the Elamites, overthrew Rim-Sin of Larsa'.
1500 BCE: Middle Elamite, the Kidinuids.
1400 BCE: the Igihalkids, 'c.
1320 BCE: Kurigalzu II 'temporarily occupied Elam around 1320 BC'.
1319 BCE: the Kassite occupation ends.
1210 BCE: the Shutrukids, 'c.
1158 BCE: Shutruk-Nakhunte conquers Babylonia.
1153 BCE: Babylonia passes to the Second Dynasty of Isin.
1100 BCE: Neo-Elamite, and three centuries of obscurity.
830 BCE: the Humban-Tahrid dynasty, 'Neo-Elamite' dynasty, 'dated c.830–521 BC'.
653 BCE: after the Battle of Ulaï (653 BC) 'Susa itself was sacked and occupied by the Assyrians'.
640 BCE: the occupation becomes annexation (next event).
640 BCE: Ashurbanipal takes Susiana (hatched occupation).
612 BCE: the Assyrian hold on Susiana ends and Elamite kings return under Median suzerainty.
539 BCE: Elam ends in the Persian empire.

wars.outcome: 'Shutruk-Nakhunte invaded Kassite Babylonia in the year 1158 BC'; 'Under his command, Elam defeated the Kassites'; Babylonia passed to the Second Dynasty of Isin from c.

wars.outcome: Sennacherib 'invad[ed] and ravag[ed] Elam' (694), Halule (691); Ashurbanipal: Ulaï (653) and the occupation of Susa, the sack of Susa (646; the Humban-Haltash page: 647, with 'I devastated the provinces of Elam and on their lands I sowed salt')…
